bound_sum_update_fn.binding: SUM construction pairs the enum state with a SumUpdateFn selected by result type. Batch update invokes that function; typed state accessors validate the matching variant outside row loops. Resize and materialization retain their enum matches. Grouped merges reuse the bound update function.

bound_aggregate_update_fns.binding: All supported aggregates pair an AccumulatorState enum with an UpdateFn during construction. COUNT, COUNT DISTINCT, AVG and COVAR_POP select fixed functions. SUM selects its typed function by result type at the same boundary, without a second indirect SUM call. MIN/MAX bind update_extremum::<true/false>, removing the stored runtime minimum flag. Each update function obtains its matching mutable state through safe private accessors outside row loops. Resize, state materialization and non-SUM/non-extremum partial merges retain enum matches. SUM and MIN/MAX merges reuse the bound update entry point.

aggregate_binding_ablation.measurement_scope: Accumulator::update only, including casts and existing row encoding; binding, resize, input creation, group-ID generation, state/output materialization, storage and pipeline scheduling excluded

aggregate_binding_ablation.conclusions: Binding alone is close to neutral at normal batches. At 8192 nullable rows, MIN/MAX Int64 direction specialization reduces time by 8.26%/5.02%; actual seven-aggregate refactor reduces mixed time by 1.69% with COUNT/Float64 SUM regressions and unstable COUNT DISTINCT. Actual source deltas include code generation and layout; do not assign them all to dispatch binding. No new full-query/DataFusion result is claimed.

closed_pr.reason: Deferred after current-source leave-one-out measurements: over 4M Snappy Parquet rows, the global Int64 SUM/COUNT query changes from 54.00 to 54.17 ms at one thread and 14.86 to 15.00 ms at four threads. Preserve the exact measured snapshots and raw samples; remove this patch from later heads. This decision applies to the measured workload and current implementation, not every possible global-SUM design.
